note_title: Credit broke first. The S&P 500 has two weeks to catch down.
note_lines: The call: over the next two weeks the S&P 500 falls about 3%, to roughly 7,510 by November 5. High-yield spreads are 66 basis points wider in six weeks while the index sits 0.8% from its record close; in all five earlier cases since 2014 with that pairing, the index was lower ten sessions later (median -3.6%).
The trade: buy SPY at-the-money puts, Nov 6 expiry (the premium is the most it can lose) - or SH, the inverse S&P 500 fund, held two weeks at most. Half size: 5 of a 100-point book.
Expected return: 3.2% on the index over two weeks (the median past case; the bar for two weeks is 0.77%). The five cases matching the signal exactly averaged 4.3%; an ordinary two weeks is +0.4%.

What kills it: an S&P 500 close above 7,818.93, the record, 0.8% above Tuesday's close. The critical review condition: high-yield spreads back under 300 basis points (333 on Oct 20) means credit has un-said it.

The other side: five cases is thin and two of them had credit moves three to five times today's; only one had the 10-year yield rising this fast; the stress is concentrated in AI-linked borrowers; hedge funds have already sold hard; and buyback windows reopen after next week's earnings.
